summary: Explains insulin concentrations (U100 and others) and how to run AAPS with non-U100 insulin. It covers the older method of a 50% modified profile and its risks, then the AAPS 4 concentration feature: enabling it, creating an insulin with another concentration in the insulin settings, switching to it at a reservoir or pod change, and recording external pen boluses. Concentration names (U100, U200) and screen labels are the app's.

sections.heading: Insulin Concentration
sections.summary: Page title and a warning that pumps are designed for U100 insulin only.

sections.heading: Reminder of the basics of insulin
sections.summary: Introduction to the basic insulin concepts that follow.

sections.heading: The insulin unit: a measure of action
sections.summary: What an international unit of insulin measures.

sections.heading: Insulin concentrations
sections.summary: The common concentrations (U100, U200 to U500, U40, diluted) and the danger of mismatched devices.

sections.heading: When using a non-standard concentration?
sections.summary: Introduction to the medical situations that need non-U100 insulin.

sections.heading: Use Case 1: diluted insulin for very low doses
sections.summary: Diluted insulin for babies and toddlers whose doses are below the pump minimum, and the safety rules for dilution.

sections.heading: Use Case 2: concentrated insulin for high insulin needs or significant insulin resistance
sections.summary: Concentrated insulin such as U200 for high insulin needs or pain from additives.

sections.heading: How to manage insulin concentration with AAPS (AAPS 3 and earlier)?
sections.summary: Introduction to the modified-profile method used before AAPS 4.

sections.heading: Using a modified profile
sections.summary: The old method: a 50% profile switch makes AAPS match U200 delivery, and the risks this creates for external boluses and reports.

sections.heading: Using the concentration parameter (new feature in AAPS 4.0)
sections.summary: Introduction to the AAPS 4 concentration feature, which keeps AAPS in real international units.

sections.heading: How it works: automatic conversion
sections.summary: AAPS keeps all data in real IU and converts values only for the pump driver.

sections.heading: Benefits and remaining risks
sections.summary: What the concentration feature fixes, and the risks that remain (relearning real values, manual pump boluses).

sections.heading: User interface display
sections.summary: Where real and concentrated units are shown: the bolus progress dialog shows IU, the pump overview shows both.

sections.heading: Enabling the feature
sections.summary: Turning on Insulin concentration support in the general settings after finishing objective 3.

sections.heading: Create a new insulin with another concentration
sections.summary: Adding an insulin with another concentration in the insulin settings: concentration, peak time, DIA and nickname, then saving.

sections.heading: Switch concentration from U100 to Uxxx (AAPS 4)
sections.summary: Switching to another concentration during a reservoir or pod change: Prime/Fill, Change, choosing the concentration and insulin, then applying the profile switch.

sections.heading: Switch concentration for users with U200 insulin associated with a 50% profile (AAPS 4)
sections.summary: Moving from the 50% profile method to the concentration feature: building a 200% profile, pausing Dynamic ISF, and switching insulin at the next change.

sections.heading: How to manage external boluses with different pens?
sections.summary: Heading for recording pen boluses with non-U100 insulin.

sections.heading: With U200 insulin associated with a 50% profile (AAPS 3)
sections.summary: With the old 50% profile, pen doses must be doubled from AAPS and halved when recorded in AAPS.

sections.heading: With U200 insulin using the concentration management included in AAPS 4
sections.summary: With the concentration feature, pen doses are recorded as given, choosing the pen insulin in the Insulin dialog.

manual_note: The page calls the insulin and profile screens "Insulin Manager" and "Profile Manager"; the app labels them "Insulin settings" and "Profile". The caption "Will be activated" was not found in the app strings.
